s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic sinusitis with destruction of nasal structures and granulomatous inflammation
salient_findings: Destruction of septal cartilage and turbinates
Growth of Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas in culture
key_facts: Male patient in his 60s
Presenting with crusting, irritation, and recurrent sinus infections
No history of hemoptysis, dyspnea, fatigue, or weight loss
No prior sinus surgeries or nasal trauma
Occasional use of nasal irrigation with tap water
Normal laboratory tests, including C-reactive protein, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, and angiotensin-converting enzyme
Negative HIV test
Substantial septal deformity with near complete destruction of the sinus septate on CT
Thinning of the posterior wall of the frontal sinuses and erosion of the bone near the right lacrimal system
Enlarged lymph nodes in the mediastinum on Chest CT
Noncaseating granulomas in sinus mucosa
Initial AFB staining was negative, but AFB PCR probe was positive

shortlist.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of noncaseating granulomas and destruction of nasal structures

shortlist.label: Tuberculosis
shortlist.why_kept: Positive AFB PCR probe and granulomatous inflammation

shortlist.label: Midline destructive granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Destruction of nasal structures and granulomatous inflammation

shortlist.label: IgG4-related disease
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation and destruction of nasal structures

raw.rationale: Positive AFB PCR probe results from both the hilar lymph node and the second FESS, despite initial negative AFB staining, strongly suggest tuberculosis infection, which can cause chronic sinus infections and granulomatous inflammation

rejected.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
rejected.why: Normal laboratory tests, including C-reactive protein and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody panel, make this less likely

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: Lack of other systemic symptoms and negative laboratory tests, such as angiotensin-converting enzyme, make this less likely

rejected.label: Midline destructive granuloma
rejected.why: Presence of positive AFB PCR probe results points towards an infectious cause rather than a destructive granuloma

rejected.label: IgG4-related disease
rejected.why: Normal laboratory tests and lack of other characteristic features, such as elevated IgG4 levels, make this less likely
